name: tokener-not-json
why: Raw bytes, not JSON at all: the tokener must fail rather than the loader dereferencing a NULL root object.
json: this is a P4 program, not a bmv2 JSON artifact

name: tokener-empty
why: Raw bytes: zero-length input. json_tokener_parse_ex() on an empty buffer returns NULL with continue-needed, which must be an error, not a wait.

name: tokener-open-brace
why: Raw bytes: a truncated document. The tokener is mid-object at end of input; a loader that ignores json_tokener_continue accepts a partial program.

name: tokener-utf8-bom
why: Raw bytes: a UTF-8 BOM (EF BB BF) before an otherwise valid document. json-c does not skip a BOM, so this must be rejected (or stripped deliberately) rather than silently truncating the first key.

name: tokener-invalid-utf8
why: Invalid UTF-8 inside a string: the "program" value carries the raw bytes 0xFF 0xFE. No JSON string can hold those, so this case is "encoding": "latin1": each code point of "json" is one byte of the document.

name: tokener-embedded-nul
why: A raw NUL byte mid-document, in the "program" value, carried as "encoding": "latin1" like the case above and passed with an explicit length. A loader that uses strlen() silently truncates everything after it.

name: tokener-top-level-string
why: Non-object top level: a bare string. JSON_TOKENER_STRICT accepts "hello" as a complete document, so our own json_object_is_type(root, json_type_object) check is what rejects it.
error: the top level must be a JSON object
json: "hello"

name: tokener-top-level-array
why: Non-object top level: an array. Same as above; the root type check, not the tokener, is the gate.
error: the top level must be a JSON object

name: tokener-trailing-garbage
why: Trailing garbage after a complete object. Without JSON_TOKENER_ALLOW_TRAILING_CHARS the tokener refuses it itself; the loader also checks json_tokener_get_parse_end() against the full input length, so a program cannot smuggle unparsed bytes past the loader.

name: tokener-two-objects
why: Two concatenated complete objects. Without JSON_TOKENER_ALLOW_TRAILING_CHARS the tokener refuses the second rather than returning after the first and reporting success.

name: tokener-deep-nesting
why: 40-deep nested arrays as a value. json-c's default depth limit is 32, so this is a tokener depth error; the loader must surface it rather than treating a NULL root as an empty program.

name: tokener-single-quoted-key
why: Raw bytes: single-quoted keys. Measured on json-c 0.18, JSON_TOKENER_STRICT ACCEPTS single-quoted strings, so the tokener returns success and this document is refused for what it lacks: "header_types".

name: tokener-bare-nan
why: Raw bytes: a bare NaN as a version element. JSON_TOKENER_STRICT ACCEPTS NaN/Infinity on json-c 0.18, yielding a json_type_double, so the version-element integer type check is what must reject it.
json: {"__meta__": {"version": [2, NaN]}}

name: meta-absent
why: No "__meta__" object at all.

name: meta-version-absent
why: "__meta__" present but with no "version".
error: '__meta__.version' must be an array of two numbers

name: meta-version-not-array
why: "version" is a string, not an array.
error: '__meta__.version' must be an array of two numbers

name: meta-version-len1
why: "version" has one element; exactly two required.
error: '__meta__.version' must be an array of two numbers

name: meta-version-len3
why: "version" has three elements; exactly two required.
error: '__meta__.version' must be an array of two numbers

name: meta-version-major-1
why: Major version 1; only major 2 is supported.

name: meta-version-major-3
why: Major version 3; only major 2 is supported.

name: meta-version-minor-256
why: Minor version 256 is outside the accepted 0..255 range.

name: meta-version-major-string
why: Major version is the string "2", not an integer. json-c will not coerce it for us unless the loader asks for get_int(), which would succeed silently.

name: caps-tables-33
why: 33 tables in one pipeline exceeds the 32-table cap. The aggregate max_size cap (P4_MAX_TOTAL_ENTRIES) is a separate bound: without it, 32 tables x 65536 entries would be ~1 GB of host heap from a few-KB document, which P4_PROGRAM_MAX does not prevent.
error: has bad or oversized tables (at most 32)

name: caps-json-cost
why: skeleton.json with an ignored key holding 65536 empty objects, which weigh 8 units each against P4_JSON_MAX_COST's 524288. json-c spends about 790 bytes of heap on an empty object, so a 4 MiB document of them would take a gigabyte; the loader weighs the document first and refuses it before json-c allocates anything. The key is one the loader ignores, so nothing else refuses it.

name: caps-table-key-136-bits
why: A table keyed on a 136-bit field. An entry carries at most 128 bits of a key, so the top byte could never be matched.
error: table 't1' matches on 'wide.w', which is 136 bits; a key field is at most 128

name: caps-action-arg-136-bits
why: An action argument of 136 bits. A table entry or default entry carries at most 128, so no control plane could set the top byte.
error: action 'set_etype' argument 0 is 136 bits, at most 128

name: caps-phv-1025-bytes
why: skeleton.json plus a 7721-bit metadata header, which rounds up to 966 bytes and brings the headers to 1025, one more than the 1024-byte packet header vector (P4_PHV_BYTES). Loaded, it would fail every frame and every RDMA operation, so the layout is checked at load.
error: the headers take 1025 bytes, more than the 1024

name: name-empty
why: A zero-length name.

name: name-newline
why: A name containing a newline. Names reach the log, so a newline lets a guest forge log lines.

name: name-ansi-escape
why: A name containing an ANSI escape sequence (ESC [ 3 1 m). Same log-forging and terminal-control risk as the newline case.

name: name-embedded-nul
why: A name with an embedded NUL, written as the \u0000 escape. json-c decodes it into the string and stores it with a length, so the string is 6 bytes but strlen() sees 3; a loader that strdup()s names compares a truncated "_dr" against the next_tables key.

name: name-field-escape
why: A header field name containing an ANSI escape. Field names are read from a tuple, not an object member, and once had their own copy of the name checks.

name: name-deparser-escape
why: A deparser order entry containing an ANSI escape. An unknown name is echoed in the refusal, so it must be refused as a name before it is looked up.
error: deparser order 0 has a bad name

name: name-next-state-newline
why: A next_state containing a newline, which would forge a log line in the 'transitions to' refusal.
error: state 'start' arm 0 has a bad next_state

name: name-field-operand-escape
why: A [header, field] operand whose field name contains an ANSI escape, which the 'does not exist' refusal would echo.
error: names a field as something other than [header, field]

name: name-extern-operand-escape
why: An extern operand naming an instance with an ANSI escape, which the 'never instantiated' refusal would echo.

name: name-expr-header-escape
why: A condition's header operand containing an ANSI escape, which the 'does not exist' refusal would echo.

name: name-expr-operator-escape
why: A condition's operator containing an ANSI escape, which the 'not supported' refusal would echo.

name: name-table-action-escape
why: A table's action list naming an action with an ANSI escape, which the 'does not exist' refusal would echo.
error: table 't1' action 1 is not a name

name: name-next-table-escape
why: A next_tables target containing an ANSI escape, which the 'not a table or condition' refusal would echo.
error: table 't1' next_tables has a bad next

name: name-next-tables-key-escape
why: A next_tables member name containing an ANSI escape. Member names never pass through a string accessor, and the 'not one of the table's actions' refusal would echo it.
error: table 't1' next_tables has an unprintable key

name: nul-select-value
why: A select arm whose value is 0x0800, a NUL and garbage. It loaded as 0x0800. json-c keeps \u0000 as a byte, and everything after it was invisible to the parser, which stopped at the NUL.
error: state 'start' transition 0 has a bad value

name: nul-select-mask
why: A select arm whose mask is 0xffff, a NUL and garbage. It loaded as 0xffff. json-c keeps \u0000 as a byte, and everything after it was invisible to the parser, which stopped at the NUL.
error: state 'start' transition 0 has a bad mask

name: nul-default-arm
why: An untyped arm whose value is 'default', a NUL and garbage. It loaded as a default arm. json-c keeps \u0000 as a byte, and everything after it was invisible to the parser, which stopped at the NUL.
error: state 'start' transition 0 has a bad value

name: nul-operand-literal
why: An assignment from the literal 0x0800, a NUL and garbage. It loaded as 0x0800. json-c keeps \u0000 as a byte, and everything after it was invisible to the parser, which stopped at the NUL.
error: 'assign' in action 'set_etype' has a malformed literal

name: nul-condition-literal
why: A condition comparing with 0x0800, a NUL and garbage. It loaded as 0x0800. json-c keeps \u0000 as a byte, and everything after it was invisible to the parser, which stopped at the NUL.

name: nul-table-key-mask
why: A table key mask of 0x00ff, a NUL and garbage. It loaded as 0x00ff. json-c keeps \u0000 as a byte, and everything after it was invisible to the parser, which stopped at the NUL.
error: table 't1' key 0 has a bad mask

name: nul-default-entry-data
why: A default entry whose argument is 0x0800, a NUL and garbage. It loaded as 0x0800. json-c keeps \u0000 as a byte, and everything after it was invisible to the parser, which stopped at the NUL.

name: nul-width-star
why: A field width of '*', a NUL and garbage: a bad width, not a variable-length field. json-c keeps \u0000 as a byte, and everything after it was invisible to the parser, which stopped at the NUL.

name: int-id-65535
why: An id of 65535, the reserved invalid-id sentinel; ids must be 0..65534.
error: header type 'ethernet_t' has a bad id

name: int-id-negative
why: A negative id.
error: header type 'ethernet_t' has a bad id

name: int-bitwidth-0
why: A field bitwidth of 0.

name: int-bitwidth-negative
why: A field bitwidth of -1. A loader that reads it into an unsigned without a range check gets 4294967295 and then allocates on it.

name: int-bitwidth-513
why: A field bitwidth of 513 exceeds the 512-bit per-field cap.

name: int-bitwidth-star
why: A bitwidth of "*", which bmv2 uses for a variable-length field. VL headers are out of the supported subset and must be rejected here, not treated as 0.

name: int-bitwidth-double
why: A bitwidth given as the double 1.0. json-c types it json_type_double; json_object_get_int() would truncate it to 1 silently.

name: int-bitwidth-string
why: A bitwidth given as the string "1". json_object_get_int() parses strings, so only an explicit json_type_int check rejects this.

name: int-bitwidth-bool
why: A bitwidth given as true. json_object_get_int() returns 1 for a boolean.

name: ref-parser-transition
why: A parser transition whose next_state names a state that does not exist.
error: transitions to 'nowhere', which does not exist

name: ref-next-table
why: A next_tables entry naming a table that does not exist.

name: ref-base-default-next
why: base_default_next names a table that does not exist. It is the table-miss target, so an unresolved one is a silently wrong forwarding decision.

name: ref-table-action
why: A table action naming an action (and an action id) not in the actions list.
error: names action 'no_such_action', which does not exist

name: ref-init-table
why: A pipeline init_table naming a table that does not exist. A non-null init_table must resolve; only null (an empty pipeline) is allowed to not.
error: starts at 't_missing', which is not one of its nodes

name: parser-two
why: Two parsers. v1model has one; which would run is a guess.

name: parser-no-states
why: A parser with no states has nowhere to start.

name: parser-dup-state
why: Two parse states with one name: a transition to it is ambiguous.

name: parser-extract-no-param
why: extract with no parameter: there is no header to extract into.
error: extract in state 'start' wants exactly one parameter

name: parser-extract-bad-param
why: extract whose parameter is not an object naming a header.
error: extract in state 'start' has a bad parameter

name: parser-extract-stack
why: extract into a header stack, which is not supported.
error: extract of a 'stack' parameter in state 'start' is not supported

name: select-key-lookahead
why: A select on a lookahead rather than a field, which is not supported.
error: select on a 'lookahead' in state 'start' is not supported

name: select-key-no-type
why: A select key with no type: what it names cannot be told.

name: select-key-not-pair
why: A field select key that is not [header, field].

name: select-key-unknown-field
why: A select on a field the header does not have.
error: selects on 'ethernet.vid', which does not exist

name: select-key-too-wide
why: A select key of 20 bytes: each field takes whole bytes of the key, and the arms are stored in 16.
error: state 'start' selects on 20 bytes, at most 16

name: select-arm-wider-than-key
why: An arm of 3 bytes against a 2-byte key: no frame could match it.
error: state 'start' transition 0 is wider than its select key

name: select-arm-bad-value
why: An arm whose value is not hex.
error: state 'start' transition 0 has a bad value

name: select-arm-negative
why: An arm whose value is negative, which no key can equal.
error: state 'start' transition 0 has a bad value

name: select-arm-number
why: An arm whose value is a JSON number rather than a hexstr.
error: state 'start' transition 0 has a non-string value

name: select-arm-valueset
why: An arm matching a parser value set, which is not supported.
error: transition of type 'parse_vset' in state 'start' is not supported

name: select-arm-mask-number
why: An arm whose mask is a JSON number rather than a hexstr.
error: state 'start' transition 0 has a bad mask

name: select-arm-mask-too-wide
why: An arm whose mask is wider than the key it masks.
error: state 'start' transition 0 has a bad mask

name: select-arm-no-value
why: An arm with no value at all, not even null.

name: select-arm-no-next-state
why: An arm with no next_state: neither another state nor accept (null).

name: select-arm-bad-next-state
why: An arm whose next_state is a number rather than a state's name.
error: state 'start' arm 0 has a bad next_state

name: select-arm-not-object
why: An arm that is not an object.
error: state 'start' transition 0 is not an object

name: deparser-two
why: Two deparsers. v1model has one; which would run is a guess.

name: deparser-order-not-name
why: A deparser order entry that is a number rather than a header's name.
error: deparser order 0 is not a name

name: dup-header-type-name
why: Two header_types with the same name; every by-name lookup becomes ambiguous.

name: dup-header-type-id
why: Two header_types with the same id.

name: dup-action-name
why: Two actions with the same name.

name: dup-table-name
why: Two tables with one name. A next, an init_table and a table update would all reach only the first.
error: two tables or conditionals are called 't1', the second in pipeline 'ingress'

name: dup-table-conditional-name
why: A conditional with a table's name. bmv2 keeps tables and conditionals in one namespace, and a next naming either would reach the first.
error: two tables or conditionals are called 't1', the second in pipeline 'ingress'

name: dup-table-name-across-pipelines
why: Ingress and egress each with a table called t1. A table update names a table, not a pipeline, so it would only ever reach ingress's.
error: two tables or conditionals are called 't1', the second in pipeline 'egress'

name: dup-table-id
why: Two tables in one pipeline with one id, which bmv2 refuses.

name: dup-conditional-id
why: Two conditionals in one pipeline with one id, which bmv2 refuses.

name: dup-pipeline-id
why: Two pipelines with one id, which bmv2 refuses.

name: cycle-two-tables
why: t1 -> t2 -> t1 via next_tables: the pipeline never terminates.

name: cycle-self
why: A table whose next_tables points at itself.

name: cycle-base-default-next
why: A cycle reachable only through base_default_next. A cycle check that walks next_tables alone misses it, and it is exactly the path a table miss takes.

name: cycle-miss
why: A cycle reachable only through the __MISS__ next_tables key.

name: cycle-conditional-false-next
why: c0 --false_next--> t1 --_drop--> c0: a cycle that closes through a conditional's false_next.

name: sem-next-tables-mixed
why: next_tables mixes __HIT__ with an action name. bmv2 keys next_tables either by action name or by __HIT__/__MISS__, never both; a mixture means the loader has to guess which convention applies.

name: sem-default-entry-arity
why: default_entry action_data has 2 elements but set_etype declares 1 runtime_data parameter; the surplus would index past the argument array.

name: sem-default-entry-too-wide
why: default_entry action_data gives set_etype's 16-bit parameter the 17-bit value 0x1ffff. A table entry that did so would be refused; the program's own default must be too, rather than truncated on every miss.
error: default argument 0 is wider than its 16-bit parameter

name: sem-runtime-data-index-oob
why: A runtime_data parameter with index 1 where the action declares 1 runtime_data entry (valid indices are 0..0). Off-by-one read of the argument array at every packet.

name: sem-primitive-not-allowed
why: The primitive "push" is not on the allow list (assign/modify_field, add/add_to_field, subtract/subtract_from_field, drop/mark_to_drop, no_op).
error: primitive 'push' in action '_drop' is not supported

name: sem-primitive-arity
why: The "assign" primitive is given 1 parameter; it takes exactly 2.

name: sem-primitive-param-type
why: A primitive parameter of type "register". Only field, hexstr, and runtime_data are supported.

name: sem-expression-operator
why: The expression operator "*" is outside the supported grammar (valid, ==, !=, <, <=, >, >=, and, or, not).

name: sem-expression-depth
why: A conditional expression nested 12 deep exceeds the depth cap; the evaluator recurses per packet, so the bound is a stack bound.

name: sem-binary-left-null
why: A binary operator with "left": null. null left is legal only for the unary ops (valid, not); for == it is a NULL dereference at evaluation time.

name: sem-table-two-lpm-keys
why: An LPM table with two LPM keys. Entries are ranked by one key's prefix, so the other's would have no say in which wins.
error: table 't1' has more than one LPM key

name: sem-table-exact-ternary-key
why: An 'exact' table with a ternary key. The lookup goes by the table's match_type, so it would take the first hit and ignore priority.
error: table 't1' matches 'exact', but its keys make it 'ternary'

name: sem-table-lpm-no-lpm-key
why: An 'lpm' table whose only key is exact: there is no prefix to rank its entries by.
error: table 't1' matches 'lpm', but its keys make it 'exact'

name: sem-table-lpm-ternary-key
why: An 'lpm' table with a ternary key beside its LPM one. p4c makes such a table ternary; ranked by prefix, it would ignore priority.
error: table 't1' matches 'lpm', but its keys make it 'ternary'

name: sem-table-ternary-no-ternary-key
why: A 'ternary' table whose keys are exact and LPM. p4c makes such a table LPM; ranked by priority, it would ignore prefix length.
error: table 't1' matches 'ternary', but its keys make it 'lpm'

name: sem-assign-from-extern
why: assign(field, <extern instance>). An extern instance has no value; the executor would read it as 0 and write that into the field on every packet.
error: 'assign' in action 'set_etype' reads an extern as a value

name: sem-valid-of-field
why: valid() of a field rather than a header. The executor would test the field for zero, not the header for validity.
error: condition 'c0': 'valid' takes a header, not a value

name: sem-not-of-value
why: not of a field rather than a boolean. bmv2's 'not' is logical; the executor would test the field for zero.
error: condition 'c0': 'not' takes a boolean, not a value

name: sem-and-of-value
why: and with a field on one side. p4c writes a boolean on both; a field would be read as true whenever it is nonzero.
error: condition 'c0': 'and' takes a boolean, not a value

name: sem-compare-header
why: A header ordered against a literal. The executor would compare the header's validity bit.
error: condition 'c0': '>' takes a value, not a header

name: sem-eq-mixed
why: == between a field and a boolean. bmv2 asserts that both sides are of one kind; the executor would compare the field with 0 or 1.
error: condition 'c0': '==' compares a value with a boolean

name: sem-eq-headers
why: == between two headers. bmv2 compares their contents, which is not built; the executor would compare their validity bits.
error: condition 'c0': '==' compares headers, which is not supported

name: sem-table-key-mask-too-wide
why: A key mask with a bit past its field. p4c writes the mask at the field's width; a wider one masks nothing there and is a different program from the one written.
error: table 't1' key 0 has a mask wider than its 16-bit field

name: sem-table-key-mask-number
why: A key mask given as a JSON number rather than a hexstr.

name: sem-table-key-mask-negative
why: A negative key mask, which p4c never writes.
error: table 't1' key 0 has a bad mask

name: sem-header-not-whole-bytes
why: A header on the wire that isn't whole bytes, which p4c refuses for bmv2. It would be extracted and emitted rounded up to a byte, taking bits of what follows it in the frame.
error: header 'ethernet' is 108 bits, which is not a whole number of bytes

name: sem-egress-spec-width
why: egress_spec declared narrower than v1model's 9-bit port. It used to resolve by name alone.

name: sem-ingress-port-width
why: ingress_port declared wider than v1model's 9-bit port. Optional, but one declared must have the architecture's width.

name: hexstr-empty
why: An empty hexstr. ernic_parse_hexstr() in src/parse_int.h is what must refuse it.

name: hexstr-prefix-only
why: A "0x" prefix with no digits. ernic_parse_hexstr() in src/parse_int.h is what must refuse it.

name: hexstr-bad-digits
why: Non-hex digits after the prefix. ernic_parse_hexstr() in src/parse_int.h is what must refuse it.

name: hexstr-minus-only
why: A lone minus sign with no digits. ernic_parse_hexstr() in src/parse_int.h is what must refuse it.

name: hexstr-minus-prefix-only
why: A negative sign and "0x" prefix with no digits. Note bmv2 hexstrs really can be negative ("-0x1" appears in simple_router.json), so the helper must accept a sign and still reject this. ernic_parse_hexstr() in src/parse_int.h is what must refuse it.

name: hexstr-wider-than-field
why: A 17-bit hexstr assigned to the 16-bit field ethernet.etherType. Must be rejected at load, not truncated at run time.
error: has a 17-bit literal for a 16-bit field
